# `set_wheel_slot_name`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Replace the filter-wheel slot names with an array of strings.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd1e20, SetSlotName @0x300e20 (64-bit build) |

Params are an array of strings in zero-based slot order. The handler reads the first child without checking that params exists or is a container, so absent, null or scalar params are unsafe and unresolved; object children are also traversed with keys ignored. Each non-string child appends error 105 but processing continues. The valid children form a map that SetSlotName accepts only when a wheel is open and the map has exactly as many entries as the current slot-name map; it then replaces the global map and persists the names. An empty array is therefore a size-dependent update or error, not a no-op. A malformed array can append several error fragments, and even later success fields, into one outer reply, so duplicate error and code members are possible; no canonical malformed-reply JSON is established.

Side effects: Replaces the in-memory slot-name map and writes it to persistent storage (SaveEFWName). No rollback and no timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_wheel_slot_name"`. [READ] |
| `params` | array<string> | yes | - | Slot names in zero-based slot order. Length must equal the current number of slots. No name-length bound and no default. [READ] |

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | A child of params is not a string (once per bad child; processing continues) | `expected string param` |
| 318 | No wheel is open | `device not connected` |
| 209 | Number of valid names differs from the current slot count | `invalid value` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Several of these can be concatenated into one reply for a malformed array; see the description.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":111,"method":"set_wheel_slot_name","params":["Dark","IR cut","Light pollution"]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_wheel_slot_name","result":0,"code":0,"id":111}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_wheel_slot_name","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":112}
```
